results.diagnosis: The add function uses subtraction operator (-) instead of addition operator (+), causing incorrect results.
The function forgot to divide discount_percent by 100 to convert the percentage to a decimal, causing it to calculate an incorrect discount amount.
The function uses > instead of >= when comparing the score to 60, causing a score of exactly 60 to return False instead of True.
The function reverses the entire string character by character instead of reversing the order of words.
The range(n) function generates 0 to n-1, but the test expects the sum of 1 to n inclusive.
Mutable default argument (items=[]) persists across function calls, causing items from previous calls to leak into subsequent calls.
The function is case-sensitive and treats different case variations of the same word as different words; it should convert words to lowercase before counting them.
The base case only checks if n == 1, but it should also handle n == 0, causing infinite recursion when factorial(0) is called.
The safe_divide function does not handle division by zero and raises a ZeroDivisionError instead of returning 0.
The function does not handle invalid input (non-numeric strings) or None values, causing ValueError and TypeError exceptions instead of returning 0 as expected.
The function uses an off-by-one error accessing items[len(items)] which is out of range; it should use items[len(items)-1] or items[-1], and return None for empty lists.
The function uses direct dictionary key access with user_dict["email"] which raises a KeyError when the key doesn't exist; it should use user_dict.get("email") to return None for missing keys.
The function uses the union operator (|) instead of the intersection operator (&) to find common elements between two lists.
The function converts the input to lowercase but fails to strip leading and trailing whitespace.
The base case checks for n == 1 but should check for n == 0, causing infinite recursion when factorial(0) is called since it keeps decrementing into negative numbers.
The while loop condition uses 'low < high' instead of 'low <= high', causing it to exit before checking the final element when low equals high.
The function crashes with ZeroDivisionError when given an empty list instead of returning 0.
The function doesn't convert the input text to lowercase, so it fails to match buzzwords with different casing like "Passionate" or "NINJA".
